clue.text: He organises room with satchels scattered

definitions.text: He organises room with satchels scattered

indicators.note: things scattered are strewn about, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A man tidies a classroom strewn with pupils' bags.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ROOM and SATCHELS, signalled by 'scattered', gives the answer, while the whole clue describes the teacher who keeps that room in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A male teacher in charge of a classroom is the man who organises that room.

clue.text: Crushed broken transport, hoisted grabbing vehicle's rear

indicators.note: in a down clue something hoisted is lifted upwards, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport

indicators.note: grabbing means the word for broken holds the next letter within it

parts.note: a dud is something broken or useless

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A wrecked bus is lifted while gripping the back of another vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crushed' looks like a description of the broken bus, but it is the definition, in the sense of beaten down in spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone crushed in spirit is quiet and cowed, which is what subdued means as an adjective.

clue.text: Employs and reportedly gives raises

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the clue words are heard rather than read, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: to give something a raise is to make it higher, so one who raises it 'highers' it

explanation.surface: A boss takes on staff and, rumour has it, hands out pay rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highers' is a playful verb form, 'makes higher', which said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ workers is to take them on for pay, the same as engaging or hiring them.

clue.text: Plump compiler's taking time to get working

indicators.note: taking means the first pieces take in another piece between their letters

parts.note: to plump for something is to opt for it
an era is a period of time
the compiler speaking of themself says I have, shortened to I've

explanation.surface: A stout crossword setter takes a while to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like an adjective, stout, but here it is the verb in 'plump for', to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something operative is in force or functioning, which is to say working.

clue.text: Flash of French fashion

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a flash of time
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A brief glimpse of what's in vogue in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a prevailing style or trend, so a synonym of fashion.

clue.text: Flag's raised initially on board ship

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting inside it, so the letter goes within the vessel's word

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A flag has been hoisted aboard a vessel at the start of a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes R from 'raised', and 'on board' places it inside STEAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant flown from a mast, a kind of flag.

clue.text: Muse captured by painter at opening

indicators.note: captured by means the letters are held within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An artist portrays a muse at a gallery's launch.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one for lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: 'Sun' issue creating agitation

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday
an edition is one issue of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A copy of the tabloid Sun newspaper stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper, which ties 'issue' to an edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedition is speech or action stirring people against authority, a form of political agitation.

clue.text: 'Fight Club' title, losing it

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport

indicators.note: losing means the following letters are dropped from the word before them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The film title Fight Club is shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fight Club' looks like one film title, but 'Fight' is the definition and 'Club' gives BAT; TITLE without IT is TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a fight between armies or opponents, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: One showing skill that's welcome in booze-up

definitions.text: One showing skill that's welcome in booze-up

indicators.note: in places the word for skill inside the word for a booze-up

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A drinks server with flair is a welcome sight at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the person behind the bar is the skilled one every drinking session welcomes.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman pouring drinks is the skilled figure every drinking session welcomes.

clue.text: Amphitheatre gripped by warfare, naturally

indicators.note: gripped by means the letters are held inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An ancient arena is naturally the scene of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is the central space of a Roman amphitheatre, and by extension the whole structure.

clue.text: Oust terrible aunts, embracing Bertie finally

indicators.note: embracing means the jumbled letters hold another letter in their midst
terrible marks the letters as made a mess of and so rearranged
finally picks out the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A young man tries to escape his fearsome aunts, as in P G Wodehouse's comic novels.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster, hero of P G Wodehouse's comic novels, is famously bullied by his aunts; 'finally' gives E, which goes inside the anagram of AUNTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat someone is to remove them from office or position, which is to oust them.

clue.text: One floats along ocean, capsizing first?

indicators.note: a capsizing boat is overturned, so these letters are upset into a new order

parts.note: first is written 1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone drifting on the sea wonders whether they'll overturn first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capsizing' makes CANOE from OCEAN; 'first' as 1ST supplies IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddler in a small light boat floats along the water, describing the answer cryptically.

clue.text: Hypocrisy of Church restrained by infinite divinity

indicators.note: restrained by means the word for church is held within the other piece
infinite means without end, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a deity is a divinity
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pious church is held back by its own boundless god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infinite' means endless, so the divinity word loses its final letter before the church abbreviation goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypocrisy is pretending to virtues one lacks, a kind of deception or double-dealing.

clue.text: Copper joining detectives to oversee English match

indicators.note: in a down clue, to oversee is to sit above, so the detectives come before the next piece

parts.note: a copper is a low-value coin
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detectives

explanation.surface: A police officer teams up with detectives to supervise an England game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that coincide agree or correspond, which is to say they match.

clue.text: Break into a sweat for each peak

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
a spire is a pointed peak on a building

explanation.surface: Climbing every summit makes a walker start sweating.
explanation.definitionFit: To perspire is to sweat, so the phrase for starting to sweat matches the verb.

clue.text: Fall about in almost relentless defeat

indicators.note: in places the laughing word inside the trimmed word
almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: stern means harsh and unyielding
to fall about is to laugh uproariously

explanation.surface: Fans fall about laughing at a heavy, unrelenting thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall about' is British idiom for laughing helplessly; 'defeat' in sport can be a slaughter, a rout.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughter in sport is a crushing, one-sided defeat.

clue.text: A receptacle like this produces plant

parts.note: a can is a container or receptacle
thus means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A container like this one yields a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produces' is a link meaning the pieces make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The acanthus is a Mediterranean plant whose leaves inspired the Corinthian column capital.

clue.text: Former wife cool about man endlessly in need

parts.note: an ex is a former wife or partner

indicators.note: about means the word for cool surrounds the trimmed piece

parts.note: ice means to cool or chill

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A frosty former wife treats a struggling man coolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' is a verb here, to chill, not an adjective describing the ex-wife.
explanation.definitionFit: An exigence is an urgent requirement or demand, so a pressing need.

clue.text: First woman barely topless with equanimity

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the top letter is taken off

parts.note: only means barely, as in only just

explanation.surface: The first woman, Eve, is barely dressed and stripped to the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' suggests nudity in Eden, but it removes the O from ONLY to leave NLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something evenly means calmly and steadily, with a level temper: equanimity.

clue.text: Erotic passage containing start of rumpy-pumpy

indicators.note: containing means the passage word holds the letter inside

parts.note: a canal is a passage or channel

indicators.note: start of picks out the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A racy passage of a book hints at sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumpy-pumpy' is British slang for sex; its first letter R goes in CANAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal means of the flesh and sexual appetite, close in sense to erotic.

clue.text: The French gossip over practically new dish

parts.note: la is French for the, in the feminine

indicators.note: over means the word is turned upside down, read from the bottom up in this down clue

parts.note: gas is idle talk or gossip

indicators.note: practically means almost all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: French chatter about a nearly new recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns GAS to SAG, and 'practically' trims NEW to NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked dish of pasta sheets layered with sauce.

clue.text: Going outside, catching cold, causing fever?

indicators.note: catching means the word for going out takes in the letter

parts.note: exiting is going out
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Going out in the cold, someone catches a chill and a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: a thrilling event causes a fever of excitement, not an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrilling stirs people to a feverish pitch of excitement, a figurative fever.

clue.text: Beat topping lead in ballroom dance

indicators.note: topping in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
having the lead is having the first go

explanation.surface: Whoever leads the ballroom dance comes out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' suggests rhythm but means to thrash, TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance that began in Argentina.

clue.text: Stones like to include entrance

indicators.note: to include means one word takes the other within it

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of similar to
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Stones are used to build an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Agates are semi-precious stones with banded colours.

clue.text: Digit's hit with end turning black

indicators.note: with end turning means the final letter is changed into another

parts.note: a thump is a hit
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A finger struck hard goes black at the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter P of THUMP becomes B.
explanation.definitionFit: The thumb is a digit of the hand.

clue.text: Surrounded in a feeble uprising

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: dim means faint or feeble

explanation.surface: A feeble revolt is surrounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' suggests a revolt, but it turns DIM upwards to MID.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid means in the middle of, that is surrounded in something.

clue.text: Taken on board and left port

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: Cargo was loaded and the ship left harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A laden vessel is loaded, its cargo taken on board.

clue.text: Stopped and hovered, smart bombs inside

indicators.note: inside means the jumbled letters go within the word for hovered

parts.note: hung means hovered, as mist hung in the air

indicators.note: bombs as a verb means explodes, so the letters are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: A drone stops and hovers, with guided munitions on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart bombs' reads as one phrase, guided weapons, but 'bombs' is the verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hamstrung is being crippled or prevented from acting, effectively stopped.

clue.text: Great band, close I fancy, covering Queen

indicators.note: covering means the jumbled letters wrap round the royal letters
fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, signalling the letters rearranged

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A great rock band, almost as fancy as Queen, plays covers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the rock band Queen, but here Queen gives the royal cipher of Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerable means large in size or amount, a synonym of great.
